title: pyproject declares a build backend that does not exist in any setuptools release, so the package cannot be installed
evidence: pyproject.toml:3 sets build-backend = "setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend". Reproduced in a temp copy: `python -m build --wheel --no-isolation` against setuptools 82.0.1 fails with `BackendUnavailable: Cannot import 'setuptools.backends._legacy'` / `ERROR Backend 'setuptools.backends._legacy:_Backend' is not available.` The module is absent in setuptools 58.0.4 and 82.0.1 (setuptools has no `backends` subpackage at all); only `setuptools.build_meta` exists. Tests still pass because pytest imports the package from the repo root rather than from an install, so the mechanical gate never exercises the backend.
suggestion: Set build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta". Without this, `pip install .` fails and the declared `brazilian-soccer-mcp` console script (pyproject.toml:24) can never be created.

title: search_players silently discards the name/nationality/position filter when the club filter is set and the prior filters matched nothing, returning the club's whole roster instead of no results
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/query_engine.py:238 — `players = [p for p in players if p.id in player_ids] if players else found`. The `if players` guard is falsy exactly when a preceding filter (name at :232, nationality at :234) has already narrowed the list to empty, so the code falls back to `found` (every player at the club) and the earlier filter is dropped. Reproduced against the real QueryEngine with a stub graph: `search_players(name="NoSuchPlayerXYZ", club="Flamengo")` returned `Found 2 player(s) matching criteria: 1. Gabriel Barbosa ... 2. Everton Ribeiro ...` instead of "No players found matching the criteria." (`search_players(nationality="Argentina", club="Flamengo")` correctly returns no players, because that intermediate list is non-empty — the bug needs an empty intermediate.)
suggestion: Drop the ternary and always intersect: `players = [p for p in players if p.id in player_ids]`. The `else found` branch has no valid case — an empty `players` list should stay empty. Add a test for a non-matching name combined with a real club.

title: 17 ruff violations in package source (11 semicolon-compound statements, 3 unused imports, 3 ambiguous variable names)
evidence: code_quality=0.6667 in scores.json. `ruff check --output-format=concise` on a temp copy of brazilian_soccer_mcp/ reports: E702 multiple-statements-on-one-line at data_loader.py:170,174,178,182,186 and query_engine.py:306(x2),308(x2),310,311; F401 unused imports `typing.Any` at knowledge_graph.py:47 and query_engine.py:26, `sys` at server.py:38; E741 ambiguous variable name `l` at query_engine.py:321,473,489.
suggestion: Run `ruff check --fix` for the 3 unused imports, split the semicolon-compound statements in the standings accumulator (query_engine.py:306-311), and rename `l` to `losses`.

title: No test combines a player-name filter with a club filter, which is why the search_players fallback bug (R8) survived a 59-test suite
evidence: tests/test_player_queries.py (98 lines) and tests/features/player_queries.feature (4 scenarios) exercise name, nationality, and club filters only in isolation; grep for a call passing both `name=` and `club=` to search_players returns nothing across tests/. All 59 tests pass (`59 passed in 8.12s`, _agent_stdout.log) with test_coverage=0.92, so the defect is invisible to the mechanical gate.
suggestion: Add a test asserting `search_players(name=<nonexistent>, club=<real club>)` reports no players found.

title: search_matches cannot restrict a match list to home-only or away-only fixtures
evidence: TASK.md:158 asks for matches 'By team (home, away, or either)'. brazilian_soccer_mcp/query_engine.py:59-63 filters with `canonical in (m.home_team, m.away_team)` — the 'either' case only — and the tool signature at server.py:81-89 exposes no venue parameter. Venue filtering does exist elsewhere (team_statistics at query_engine.py:162 and best_records at :439 both accept venue="home"/"away"), which is what satisfies R3's pinned how_to_verify and TASK.md's 'What is Corinthians' home record in 2022?' example.
suggestion: Add a `venue` parameter to search_matches mirroring team_statistics, so raw match listings can be narrowed to home or away fixtures.

title: Cross-dataset de-duplication protects standings from double-counting overlapping season data
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp/data_loader.py module docstring (:15-24) plus `_load_novo` (drops seasons >= 2012 that overlap Brasileirao_Matches.csv) and `_load_br_football` (skips any (competition, season) pair already supplied by a primary source). The five supplied match CSVs have overlapping coverage, so an unguarded load would inflate standings points.
suggestion: None — this is beyond-spec correctness work worth surfacing for cross-run comparison.
